prompt: hi, weekly status for the gpu cluster upgrade. we migrated node-07 to the new firmware stack on tuesday, took about 4 hours, no data loss. node-12 is blocked, firmware mismatch between the bmc and the gpu driver, vendor says new bmc image is due 2/14 but that's not firm. all other nodes are still on the old stack. we have a go/no-go for full cutover scheduled for friday 2/9, but i'm not sure we can make it if node-12 isn't resolved. also need to decide if we cut over the remaining 14 nodes in one window or stagger them. the director of engineering will read this and needs to approve the cutover plan or delay it. we haven't decided on a fallback if the vendor misses the date.

vp of sales, quick update on the crm cleanup. we deduplicated 3,847 records last week, mainly accounts and contacts. found one territory boundary error: the north region has 12 accounts that should be in south per the 2023 map. that's about 2.1m in pipeline affected. we also flagged 15% of records with missing phone numbers, not blocking but annoying for the field team. the big question is the data-quality vendor. we got two bids, one is 40k for a one-time scrub, the other is 15k per quarter for ongoing. we need a decision by 2/15 to include it in the next budget cycle. you'll read this and decide which vendor to go with, or if we skip it and do manual cleanup. i don't have a strong preference yet, need to see the sla details.

daily project update for the tracker. rate-limit change for the public api is in progress. we migrated the mobile client to the new limit (1000 req/hr) yesterday, no issues. the web client is still on the old limit (500 req/hr). we have a rollout date of 3/1 for the full switch, but that might slip because the web team has a release freeze until 3/15. also, some partners haven't confirmed they can handle the lower limit. we tested 3 partners, 2 passed, 1 failed with 429s. not sure if we need to give that partner an exception or they fix their code. the tracker is read by the project sponsor and the dev lead, they need to approve the final rollout date and the exception policy. no recommendation from me yet.

status for the head of learning on the course-authoring tool rollout. we converted 23 out of 25 courses from the old format to the new one. the remaining 2 courses have a file-format issue, the video embeds are in .wmv and the new tool only supports .mp4. we tried to convert them with the built-in converter, but it crashes on files larger than 2gb, and one course has a 3.2gb video. we're looking at a third-party converter, costs about 500 per course, but we need to decide if we buy that or ask the course authors to re-record the videos. the head of learning will read this and decide on the converter purchase or a re-recording effort. the rollout deadline is 4/1, so we have some time, but not much. also, one course has outdated content, not sure if we should update it now or after the rollout.

weekly update to the director of product on the user-research panel. we recruited 34 participants for the new dashboard study, target is 40. we have good coverage across the west and east regions, but the midwest segment is underrepresented, only 4 participants vs the 10 we wanted. we've tried social media and email, but the response rate is low there. we're thinking of offering a higher incentive for that group, maybe 75 instead of 50, but that's a budget decision. the director will read this and decide if we increase the incentive or adjust the study scope. the study starts 2/20, so we need a decision by 2/12. also, we haven't finalized the screening questions, but that's a minor thing. we have 2 participants who might drop out, so we need a buffer.

handoff note for the next on-call. slow certificate-revocation check, ticket #4821. we ruled out network issues, the crl endpoint responds in 200ms from our side. we also ruled out a bad ocsp responder, tested with openssl and it's fine. current state: the check takes 30 seconds to complete, but it should be under 5. we suspect the local cache is corrupted, but we haven't cleared it yet because that might cause a brief outage. we also found a log entry at 14:32 that shows a timeout, but not sure if that's related. next verification time is unknown, we were waiting for the certificate to expire, but it's a 90-day cert, so it's not expiring soon. the next on-call needs to decide if we clear the cache or wait for the vendor to respond. they should also check if the cert is used in any critical path. no action taken yet, just monitoring.

cfo, update on the software-amortization schedule. we capitalized 1.2m in development costs for project phoenix in q1. the project is behind on milestones, we expected to hit the beta milestone by 1/31, but it's now 2/5 and we're at 80% feature completion. the remaining 20% is a payment module that's proving complex. we need to decide if we do an impairment review now or wait until the next quarter. the gaap rules say we should assess if the asset is recoverable, but we don't have enough data yet. also, we have 3 other projects that are on track, so it's just phoenix. the cfo will read this and decide on the impairment review and if we need to adjust the amortization period. we haven't discussed the discount rate for the recoverability test, that's open. the schedule is due for the audit in april, so we have some time.

sprint-end summary for the team lead on the refactoring. we split the monolith into 5 modules, as planned. modules A, B, C, and E are clean, no circular dependencies. module D has a dependency cycle with module B, it's a 2-cycle where D calls B and B calls D in a specific error path. we've documented it, but it's ugly. we have two options: extract the shared logic into a new module, which would take about 3 days, or leave it as is and add a comment. the team lead will read this and decide which way to go. we also reduced the test execution time from 45 minutes to 18 minutes, which is good. the code coverage is at 82%, up from 74%. we didn't touch the legacy payment code, that's out of scope. next sprint is for the new feature, so this cycle needs to be closed.

head of security, phishing-simulation campaign results are in. we sent 2,000 emails across 5 departments. overall click rate was 12%, which is down from 18% last quarter. by department: engineering 5%, sales 18%, marketing 10%, hr 8%, finance 15%. the sales team failed repeatedly, this is the third time they've had the highest click rate. we have a policy that says if a team fails more than twice, they need mandatory retraining, but we haven't enforced it yet. the head of security will read this and decide if we enforce the retraining for sales, and if we need to change the simulation cadence for them. also, we had 3 people who reported the phishing email, which is good, but we didn't track who they were. we're not sure if the lower overall rate is due to better awareness or because we used a less convincing template this time. no recommendation from me.

daily update for the tracker on the backup-and-restore test. we verified restores for two systems, the crm and the billing system, both completed in under 2 hours, data integrity checks passed. the database restore for the analytics system failed, it errored out at 45% with a checksum mismatch. we're not sure if it's a corrupted backup or a storage issue. we're going to run a root-cause analysis, but that's pending, we haven't started yet. the tracker is read by the it manager and the compliance officer, they need to decide if we go live with the new backup solution next week or wait for the rca. the test window ends 2/16, so we have 3 days to resolve. we also noticed that the backup size for the analytics system is 30% larger than expected, but that might be normal. no action taken yet, just reporting.
